A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same 28-page research work, including Sections 1–6 and Appendices A–D. The text, equations, and algorithm displays are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 presents theoretical algorithms, reductions, regret guarantees, and proofs. Inspection of the main text and appendices establishes that no original empirical results are reported.

after.justification: v3 remains entirely theoretical, including its appendices. It reports no experimental, simulation, user-study, or data-analysis outcomes.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–5 retain their updates, regularizers, learning-rate grid, and reductions. Explicitly ending Algorithms 3–5 at T clarifies the already stated T-round setting rather than changing the method.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or conducts empirical task evaluations. Movement costs, delayed feedback, and time-varying memory remain the same theoretical applications.

E2.justification: The same prior methods appear in theoretical regret-bound comparisons, including Wan et al. (2024) and Zhao et al. (2023). Neither version adds or removes an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: No empirical evaluation protocols or experimental settings are reported in either version. The formal online interaction and feedback protocols are retained.

E4.justification: Neither version contains ablations, sensitivity tests, robustness experiments, or empirical case studies. The appendix material remains theoretical derivations and proofs.

E5.justification: Repeated runs, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, and other empirical uncertainty reporting are absent from both versions.

E6.justification: Neither version contains empirical result entries. The reported regret guarantees and qualitative comparisons with prior bounds remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix B, Equation (18), replaces an incorrect equality with an inequality when extending a within-epoch sum to all rounds. Lemma D.1 now handles P=0 or V=0 separately and replaces exact doubling with an inequality appropriate to the capped learning-rate grid. These are limited proof repairs; theorem statements remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about comparator-adaptive dynamic regret, time-varying movement costs, and reductions for delayed feedback and memory. The claimed guarantees and contribution scope are unchanged.

C2.justification: The explanations of adaptive batching, first-order movement-cost dependence, and application reductions are retained. Qualifications concerning prior knowledge, feedback, memory lengths, and comparisons with existing guarantees are unchanged.

D1.justification: Algorithm parameters and technical specifications are retained. Adding 'when working in R^d' to the existing O(d log T) complexity statement clarifies notation; no implementation or code/data access information is added.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged. Reference edits correct capitalization and author-name accents rather than adding or replacing sources.

P1.justification: v3 makes scattered grammar, citation-style, and notation edits, removes a redundant proof pointer, and adds descriptive subtitles to Appendices A–C. The section order and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Mathematical delimiters, pseudocode loop lines, and local line and column breaks receive small typesetting adjustments. The five algorithm displays retain their locations, and no figures or tables are added or removed.

improvement.justification: v3 improves mathematical precision by correcting Equation (18) and closing the zero-case and capped-grid gaps in Lemma D.1. Clearer appendix headings and small editorial corrections also help readability. These are useful, limited repairs that preserve the paper's methods, scope, and principal guarantees.
